module_title: Structure of the Modern Table and Chemical Families
introduction: The modern periodic table is like a massive multi-story apartment building. It has horizontal rows and vertical columns. At this level, we understand its 'blocks' and the 'families' that live in it.

core_concepts.title: Periods and Groups
core_concepts.description:
1. Periods: There are 7 horizontal rows. The period number tells you the number of 'Shells/Orbits' the elements in that row have. 
2. Groups: There are 18 vertical columns. Elements in the same group have the exact same number of 'Valence Electrons', meaning they have similar chemical properties.

core_concepts.title: The Four Blocks (s, p, d, f)
core_concepts.description:
1. s-block: Groups 1 and 2 (Highly reactive light metals). 
2. p-block: Groups 13 to 18 (Contains metals, non-metals, and metalloids). 
3. d-block: Groups 3 to 12. These are called 'Transition Elements' (heavy, hard metals like Iron, Gold). 
4. f-block: The two separate rows at the bottom. These are 'Inner Transition Elements' (Lanthanides and Actinides).

core_concepts.title: Important Chemical Families
core_concepts.description:
1. Group 1: Alkali Metals (e.g., Na, K). Extremely reactive, stored in kerosene. 
2. Group 2: Alkaline Earth Metals (e.g., Mg, Ca). 
3. Group 17: Halogens (F, Cl, Br, I). The most reactive non-metals. 'Halogen' means salt-producing. 
4. Group 18: Noble Gases (He, Ne, Ar). Inert and unreactive because their outermost shell is completely full.

important_entities.name: The Metalloid Zig-zag Line
important_entities.significance: In the p-block, there is a zig-zag line. To its left are Metals, and to its right are Non-metals. The elements situated exactly on this line are 'Metalloids' (e.g., Boron, Silicon, Germanium), which show properties of both.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Which group does Hydrogen belong to? It is placed in Group 1 for convenience (because it has 1 valence electron), but its properties also match Group 17 (Halogens). Hence, it is called the 'Rogue Element' of the periodic table with no truly fixed position.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Group 11 elements are called 'Coinage Metals' because they were used to make coins in ancient times.

exam_strategy_tips: Railway Exams frequently ask: 'What are Group 18 elements called?' Answer: Noble gases or Inert gases.
